extracted.intended_audience: researchers who are applying for or conducting research funded by the KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research) program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for applying to, managing, spending, reporting, and complying with Japan's KAKENHI research grants (MEXT/JSPS). Covers eligibility, review, budgeting (direct/indirect), modifications, assessments, ethics, and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI provides financial support for creative and pioneering research conducted by individual researchers; the contents of the research proposal must be original planned by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose research based on their own original ideas; KAKENHI funds curiosity-driven to mission-oriented research but prioritizes researcher-initiated originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of application, applicants must belong to a research institution and meet requirements a) job assignment includes research activity, b) actually engaged in research activity (not only research-assisting jobs), and c) must not be a graduate student or other student status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research institutions must recognize the applicant as meeting the conditions and register the applicant in e-Rad as eligible. JSPS Research Fellows (DC) are treated as eligible in certain cases—confirm with the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility due to penalties or misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual must not be categorized as ineligible for grant acquisition in the fiscal year covered by the call (penalty for fraudulent grant acquisition, improper spending, or misconduct using KAKENHI or other competitive funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm they are not subject to active restrictions or penalties before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three mandatory pre-application actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, applicants must (1) ascertain eligibility for KAKENHI application, (2) confirm researcher information registered in e-Rad (managed by the research institution), and (3) obtain an e-Rad ID and password from their research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps are required to ensure application processing; contact the e-Rad administrator at your institution for registration/revision procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of unreasonable duplication and parallel submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying for multiple research projects, eliminate unreasonable duplications and excessive concentration, and avoid violating restrictions on parallel submission of research proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Application Procedures for specific restrictions per category; research institutions may set additional rules. Parallel applications for carried-over single-year projects and new proposals may be allowed in some cases—confirm specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and prescribed application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid errors or omissions in filling out the application form; the format of application documents may not be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to numeric budget digits, project title spelling, and other details. Follow the prescribed forms exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and institutional approval for Co-Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding a Co-Investigator to the Project Members List, obtain the consent of the prospective Co-Investigator and their research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in project roles (e.g., Co-Investigator to Collaborating Researcher) can be treated as removal and may require procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on use of generative AI in application preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of generative AI in preparing application documents carries risks of inadvertent copyright infringement and leakage of personal/confidential information; it is the researcher's responsibility to decide appropriate usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should manage confidentiality and copyright risks when using AI tools and ensure final submissions meet originality and confidentiality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of research team roles and fund rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator: full responsibility for implementation; Co-Investigator: carries out project with PI and receives a share of funds usable at their discretion; Research Collaborator: cooperates but is not a funded project member and does not have discretion over funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even individuals ineligible to apply can be Research Collaborators. Role changes may have procedural implications for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of other funding, positions and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must enter in the application and e-Rad their current domestic and foreign research funding (competitive funds, private subsidies, company funds), organizations they belong to, current positions including concurrent positions and foreign recruitment programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and accurate disclosure is required for transparency and review; see Supplement to Application Procedures for form details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review selection and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI selects projects via peer review involving prominent researchers; JSPS uses a reviewer candidate database largely of prior KAKENHI-funded researchers and discloses review committee member names on the website after review completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers are asked to participate in the review process; selection of high-quality committee members and transparency measures are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and oversight of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS verifies and analyzes review fairness (e.g., favoritism, adherence to review rules); committee members found dispensing favors or conducting improper reviews may be excluded from future reviewer selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings from audits influence future reviewer selection and are taken into account appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of review results and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on research category, JSPS discloses information such as approximate ranking, opinions in review results, rating-element results and standard-format opinions (some items disclosed for non-adopted projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the JSPS KAKENHI website for what is published per category; disclosure differs by category (e.g., S/A vs B/C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date and use of funds tied to provisional grant decision
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI funding can be used after the notice of provisional grant decision; research start dates are usually April 1 (new/continued projects) except where provisional decision dates differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary contracts can be signed and activities started after provisional decision even if funds have not yet been disbursed; disbursement timing varies (e.g., first-term remittance around July).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research institution management obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and procedures for KAKENHI are carried out by research institutions to reduce researcher burden and prevent inadvertent rule violations; researchers must follow institution accounting rules and Supplementary/Funding Conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the person in charge at your institution for clarifications on purchasing, payments, and fund use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted direct expenses (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expense can be used broadly for expenses necessary to carry out the research project, including purchase of goods, travel expenses, personnel costs/honoraria (subject to restrictions), and miscellaneous expenses; includes compiling research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct expense use should be socially acceptable and prioritized appropriately; Principal Investigator and Co-Investigators are accountable for spending judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct expense exclusions and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Items not recognized as direct expense include costs for buildings and facilities (except necessary installation costs), costs for handling accidents/disasters during research, personnel costs/honoraria for the Principal Investigator or Co-Investigator(s), and other costs that should be covered by indirect expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Spending Rules for full lists and examples. Institutional accounting rules and Spending Rules determine acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social acceptability and PI accountability for spending
rubrics_metrics.description: When using research grants, researchers should consider whether payments are socially acceptable and whether the priority of direct expense use is appropriate; PI and Co-Investigators must take accountability for spending decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should align with Spending Rules, institutional regulations, and reasonable public expectations for use of public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining direct expenses with other funds and demarcation
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expenses may be combined with other funds (non-KAKENHI or other KAKENHI funds) under conditions: objective identification of amounts or rational basis for allocation, and identification of expenditure demarcation or cost-burden basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: separating one-way vs round-trip travel, purchased quantities, estimated percentage of use, number of projects, or estimated project period as rational bases. Consult institution for combined-use procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint-use purchase and shared facilities guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities and equipment purchased with direct expenses that meet conditions (purchase price ≥10 million yen, general-purpose, no risk of interfering with funded project) should be jointly used within/outside the institution via institutional joint-use systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Guidelines toward Promotion of Joint Use of Research Facilities and Equipment (Mar 2022). Joint-use should not interfere with the implementing funded project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect expense rate and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect expense is delivered to research institutions at a fixed ratio to direct expense — the amount equivalent to 30% of the direct expense — and is for supporting research activities and upgrading the research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect expenses can be used by institutions for personnel costs (including PI/Co-Investigator), technical staff for shared equipment, facility management, patent fees, equipment costs, library costs, journal subscriptions/article charges, consumables, publicity, patent attorney fees, and similar institutional research-support purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor modifications allowed without JSPS application/notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on research progress, certain changes may be made without applying to JSPS, e.g., changing allocation among direct expense cost items within 50% of total direct expense (or up to ¥3 million if 50% is ≤¥3 million); partial changes within original research objectives (roles, allocation shares, schedule, major goods breakdown) are expected as long as within objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be made appropriately to achieve original research objectives. The 50% rule uses decided expense amount per fiscal year (Single-year) or entire research period (Multi-year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes requiring procedures and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes that require prior procedures include major allocation changes exceeding 50% of total direct expense (or >¥3 million threshold), addition/removal of a Co-Investigator, extension of research period due to maternity/childcare leave or research stay abroad, change in research institution (which may prevent continuation of funding), and extension of funded project period (procedures differ by fund type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the formal procedures and notifications for each change type. Multi-year Funds can in some cases be extended for one year via acceptance procedures during the last year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of Single-year Grants spending and carryover rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-year Grants are decided per fiscal year; research grants must be used by end of fiscal year though carryover to next fiscal year is possible if conditions are met and carryover procedures followed. Adjustment Funds may allow use ahead of schedule or carryover subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MEXT/JSPS pages on carryover and Adjustment Funds for details. Carried-over projects can still apply in parallel for new proposals in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year Funds budgeting and spending flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-year Funds are budgeted at one time for the entire research period; grants can be used across fiscal years according to research progress without strict fiscal year division; unused funds may be used in subsequent fiscal years within the funded period without prior carryover procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goods can be purchased over multiple fiscal years. Check which categories are Multi-year Fund eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim and ex-post assessments; disclosure of results and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment or third-party assessments (interim/ex-post) are performed; JSPS discloses Report on Research Achievements (PDF), opinions in review results, and results of assessments per category and schedule (timing varies by category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Research Outline' from the formal application is publicly disclosed to inform the public. Research papers may be linked via DOI in KAKEN. Posting schedules are tentative and category-dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment and indication of KAKENHI support in outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing research achievements obtained using KAKENHI, researchers must indicate the support and include 'JP' plus the 8-digit JSPS/MEXT KAKENHI Grant Number in acknowledgments or designated section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formats provided: 'This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP12K34567.' For multiple grants list multiple JPxxxxxxxx entries. Use the specified English/Japanese phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access requirement and research data management
rubrics_metrics.description: From calls after April 2025, academic papers and supporting data must be posted in an infrastructure (e.g., institutional repositories) immediately after publication; report open access status in implementation and results reports. JSPS promotes data management plans (DMPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow JSPS guidance on open access and data handling; report compliance in required reports. Links to JSPS OA and DMP guidance are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of KAKENHI logo and public presentation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When announcing achievements at meetings or public venues, researchers should use the KAKENHI logo whenever possible (downloadable from MEXT/JSPS websites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow logo usage guidance on the MEXT/JSPS sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher information registration and researchmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers are requested to actively register researcher information and research achievements in 'researchmap'; this is linked to e-Rad and used in the KAKENHI review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active registration facilitates dissemination and may be used in reviews; researchmap is one of the largest Japanese researcher databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for rule violations (improper spending, fraud, misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations such as improper grant spending, fraudulent grant acquisition, and research misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) can result in return of funds (part or all), suspension of KAKENHI for 1–10 years (depending on offense), public disclosure of outlines and names, suspension of funding for adopted projects, and restrictions on other funding participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties vary by offense type and severity; conspirators may also be penalized. Institutions and JSPS/MEXT handle enforcement and public disclosure in principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct and basic responsibilities for scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists shall assure the quality of knowledge they create, act with honesty and integrity, maintain expertise, consider societal impacts, disclose results and evaluations, and be mindful of possible dual use and appropriate means of publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Science Council of Japan Code of Conduct and JSPS materials like 'For the Sound Development of Science' for more detailed behavioral and ethical expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory participation in research ethics/compliance education
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators and Co-Investigators must participate in research ethics education and compliance education provided by their institutions; participation status will be confirmed at formal application for grant delivery and request for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use JSPS-provided materials and e-learning (eL CoRE) as appropriate and maintain participation records for formal application steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency obligations to prevent conflicts of interest and undue influence
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-Is are required to enter information on non-competitive research funds, competitive funds not entered in e-Rad, concurrent positions, participation in foreign recruitment programs, donations, and supports other than monetary funds to ensure transparency; failure to report can prevent application eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report these transparently via e-Rad 'Modify Researcher Details' page and institutional procedures. Failure to pledge that reports were made can block application capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with research-specific laws/guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on research content, procedures may be required under laws/guidelines (e.g., ethical guidelines for human-subjects research, acts/guidelines on human embryos, guidelines for embryonic stem cells, gene therapy clinical trials, biosafety acts, animal experiment guidelines, foreign exchange/export control laws, access to genetic resources, personal information protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify applicable laws/guidelines for your research plan and follow required procedures in addition to KAKENHI rules; consult institutional compliance units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiries should be routed via research institution with official contacts provided
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, inquiries regarding KAKENHI should be made through the research institution; official contact points at MEXT and JSPS (addresses, telephone numbers, URLs) are provided for additional assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional administrative offices for day-to-day questions; use MEXT/JSPS contacts for unresolved or program-level inquiries.
